#1352. Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” said Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

#1350. Parma lose Romero for rest of 2026 after serious shoulder injury

Parma are not expected to have centre-forward David Romero back in action before 2027, as he has been diagnosed with a serious shoulder injury.

The centre-forward fell awkwardly during the most recent Serie A match against Bologna and had to be substituted.

According to Sky Sport Italia, the player had specialist tests that confirmed this was not a normal dislocation.

It is an acromioclavicular subluxation and will require at least six weeks on the sidelines, meaning Parma won’t have Romero back before Christmas and the break for the holidays.

The 23-year-old Argentine was a big investment from Tigre over the summer at €7m and he had a good start, scoring two goals in nine Serie A appearances.

His absence could give Italy Under-21 international striker Simone Lontani more playing time at the Stadio Tardini.

Meanwhile, Diego Carlos was also diagnosed with a muscular strain in his left thigh following Saturday’s 2-0 friendly win over Cesena.

This puts him in doubt for this weekend’s return to Serie A action against Roma on Saturday evening.

Chelsea are reportedly going to be one to watch in the race to sign Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi in the upcoming January transfer window.

The 20-year-old is one of the most exciting young talents in the game right now, having scored a superb 13 Premier League goals last season to fire Bournemouth into Europe.

It now seems inevitable that the Cherries are going to lose Kroupi to a big name, and Simon Phillips reports that Chelsea are keen on him alongside his club teammate Alex Scott.

There’s also a clear role for Kroupi in this Gunners side as they lack a genuine star name in their front three, with Kroupi surely an upgrade on the likes of Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz, and Christos Tzolis.

#1347. Galliani would ‘absolutely’ back Mancini as Italy coach if FIGC President

Adriano Galliani reveals who convinced him to run for FIGC President and assures he will ‘absolutely’ stick with Italy coach Roberto Mancini if replacing Giovanni Malagò.

The Italian Football Federation was thrown into chaos last month when it was ruled that Malagò did not have the requisite paperwork when he first ran for President, so his June landslide election was null and void.

Faced with the need to put the FIGC under a Special Commissioner until the next election on December 14, the CONI (Italian Olympic Committee) decided to give the role to Malagò.

At the time, it was assumed this would be just a stopgap solution until he could be elected properly, but former Milan and Monza CEO Galliani threw his hat into the ring.

“There are two candidates, the vote is in four weeks, so we’ll see what happens,” Galliani told Sky Sport Italia.

“I was convinced by some phone calls from clubs, but also from the Players’ Association and Coaches’ Association. I had said no in the past, but (Coaches’ Association President) Renzo Ulivieri told me that the rapport with the Lega Calcio was at its best when I was President. Umberto Calcagno told me the same thing.

“I have a very long and detailed proposal for my tenure, which I have already presented and deposited.”

There was the risk of further chaos when Galliani’s lawyer had presented an appeal against Malagò running for FIGC President again, because there was confusion over who had the right to propose him from Genoa.

However, that was dropped just before the deadline, so the election will go ahead on December 14.

“I told my lawyer to let it go, Italian football already has so many problems,” explained Galliani.

“I spent 50 years in Italian football, there are too many things to sort out, and I wrote them all in my plan.”

The major decision made by Malagò as FIGC President was to appoint Mancini as the Italy coach, so is that something Galliani would confirm if he won the election?

#1346. Jarrad Branthwaite left out of England squad for Nations League decider with Spain - as James Hill and Dan Burn leapfrog defender in Thomas Tuchel's pecking order

Published: 10:05 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 15 November 2026

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ said the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and said: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order

Branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

#1345. Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding new ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

Chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv

That should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

He signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Caicedo rattles the woodwork with a stunning effort! 💥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/CSIM9ogtSp

Rogers’s reprieve changed all that. Inexplicably inconsistent as Tierney was, Chelsea exhibited a steel which thrilled Alonso as much as those games when Cole Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are in full flow.

“They didn’t score, but did a fantastic job for the team,” Alonso pointedly said of his attackers.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s new home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.

He told TNT Sports: “We were a little bit unlucky with the goals. It wasn’t good defending, but it takes a couple of deflections before it gets to Neto. It makes it a relatively easy finish for him.

“The second one was a free-kick which obviously ricochets around, so I think there were parts of the game we did OK, but we didn’t offer enough to create enough, to make enough chances. I can’t think of many, so that is probably the biggest indictment.”

He had a minor gripe over a first-half tackle that was reviewed, saying, “I think the Morgan Rogers tackle on Jimmy [Garner] could have been questioned.”

However, given the good start to the season for Everton so far, he does not have too much rancour.

He describes the planned tests as “precautionary” and says, “as far as I know, he left the stadium conscious.”

Neto added more detail to his thoughts on the game.

On his first goal, he explained how Everton’s defensive approach allowed them to react: “We know that they came man-to man. In the second half we adjusted some stuff. We tried to get the best of the man-to-man press and we got away. We got the cross and I could finish well, so really happy.”

He credited his Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, with his calmness in front of goal, adding: “This comes a little bit from the new coach of the national team that says when you are near to the area you need to pass to the goal, so really happy with that.”

With Chelsea now in the Champions League places, Neto was keen to keep up the momentum. He said: “It’s really important. We know it’s tough to play away, even at home there are no easy games. We came here with personality, with good intentions to win the match and really happy with the result.”

Chelsea captain Reece James’ surgery could be out for a couple of months, Xabi Alonso explained.

He told the  press: “I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks. It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.”

He is looking to vice captains Moises Caceido and Levi Colwill to step up in his absence, explaining: “You can be a captain without an armband, for sure. Leadership is important and that’s why we have this group, not just on matchday.”

James remains vital to Chelsea at their best, and while his minutes have been managed, it’s a huge disappointment to see him need to go under the knife once more.

We have not got too many players. I am not saying we’re going to win the league, but we want to try to challenge and be around the top teams.”

That might be made harder by the news that the Friedkin Group are already looking to sell the club after only a couple of years in charge. Moyes is a rare thing, a manager who keeps improving despite setbacks, and his second spell has been fairly solid so far.

Moyes is aware that Chelsea pose a threat up front, adding: “Their attacking line is incredibly exciting. I also think they have got some super defenders as well, but they are playing quite an expansive game, which on its day can lead to goals and on another day it can lead to defeats.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

Next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

#1344. Caprile on Cagliari chance, Conte anger and Albania opportunity

Elia Caprile has been the most effective goalkeeper in Serie A this season at Cagliari, but reveals Antonio Conte ‘did not take it well’ when he left Napoli, is open to playing for Albania, and nearly gave up his career.

The 25-year-old has kept four clean sheets in 11 Serie A games so far this season, more than any other goalkeeper in the division, and also made more saves than anyone else.

Despite that, he knows that he’s very far behind in the ranking for Italy, where Gianluigi Donnarumma, Guglielmo Vicario, Marco Carnesecchi and Alex Meret are all ahead of him.

“I would love to silence all those who wouldn’t bet a cent on me when I was little, that fire inside me is still burning,” Caprile told the Corriere della Sera newspaper.

“I thought of quitting so many times, especially when a few coaches were mean to me. I wasn’t playing, I was shorter than the other kids, I was fat.

“I was made to feel bad about it and lost my way, but I got advice from two goalkeeping coaches Bressan and Squizzi at the moment I needed them the most. They showed me football is made of sacrifice, both before and after training.”

Caprile has never played for Italy at senior level, and now has Albanian citizenship thanks to his partner.

“I don’t know if something can come from it, so far no Federation has knocked at my door. If they do, then I will evaluate.”

He already made the decision to walk away from Napoli in 2025 when frustrated at the lack of playing time, and took the opportunity to shine at Cagliari.

“Conte told me to stay and fight for my place with Meret, so he was honest, and so was I. He chose Alex and won the Scudetto, so it was wise, but I was 23 and really wanted to play. I felt the physical need to be on the pitch,” explained Caprile.

“So in January, I told him I wanted to leave. Conte did not take it well, but he understood.”

#1342. Every Arsenal Player's Wages [2026]

Arsenal have been on a meteoric rise back to the top of the Premier League under Mikel Arteta in the past few years. The Gunners haven't been shy about spending big sums of money to get back to the top, though, and this is shown in their wage bill.

The reigning English champions have signed some of the biggest stars around in recent transfer windows and have also splashed the cash on securing long-term deals for their most important assets.

Amid those key developments within the squad, below is a full list of the Arsenal players' wages – including the reported salaries of key summer signings Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa.

David Raya's move from Brentford to Arsenal was made permanent during the summer of 2024, following an excellent spell between the sticks for the north Londoners, where he won the Golden Glove. After signing new terms in October 2025, the Spanish shot-stopper is now pocketing £100,000 per week after proving himself among the best goalkeepers in the business.

The Gunners managed to shift Aaron Ramsdale's substantial £100,000-per-week salary off their books, selling their back-up goalkeeper to Southampton in 2024. In his place, Kepa Arrizabalaga, following loan stints at Real Madrid and Bournemouth, joined from Chelsea, and he earns £60,000 every seven days as a result.

Arsenal won the race to sign Illan Meslier on a free transfer this summer after his contract with Leeds United expired. The Frenchman was highly rated at the beginning of his career but has struggled in recent years. Despite losing his place as Leeds' starting goalkeeper, he was handed a £45,000-per-week deal by the Gunners.

William Saliba and Gabriel have grown to be the best central defensive partnership in the English top flight. The duo have been equally impressive on the pitch in four successive title charges - with the most recent being successful - and they've both been rewarded with big contracts in recent times.

Gabriel is earning £180,000-per-week, while Saliba has more recently put pen-to-paper on a five-year deal worth £270,000-per-week.

Summer signing Ezri Konsa earns the same amount as Gabriel, and just more than Ben White. The latter spent much of last season sidelined through injury, and has had a fight on his hands to re-establish himself as a regular starter.

From Liverpool to Aston Villa, the next 25 winners of the Premier League have been predicted by AI.

Arsenal confirmed the arrival of Riccardo Calafiori from Bologna in the summer of 2025, with the Italian defender earning £140,000 every seven days. Piero Hincapie enjoyed a successful loan spell at the Emirates, and is now earning £120,000 weekly after making his move permanent.

Jurrien Timber earns the same amount as the Ecuadorian, though he is in line for a pay rise after his contributions last term, which saw him fill in all across the backline where key injuries left some gaping holes. It is believed he has agreed a contract extension, although it is not yet known how much he will earn when he puts pen-to-paper.

The highly-rated Cristhian Mosquera, signed from Valencia last summer, is earning £70,000-per-week at the club. Still just 22 years old, he could be a key player for the club for many years to come.

Breakthrough talent Myles Lewis-Skelly is one of the highest-earning teenagers in world football. He put pen-to-paper on a five-year contract worth £50,000-per-week last summer, a cool sum for someone who is still in the infancy of his career.

Arsenal, despite having one of the best midfields in the world, thought they needed to strengthen the area further after winning the Premier League in 2026. They went all out for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, with the Brazilian joining the English champions in a £75m move. He penned a four-year deal (with an option of an extra year) worth £250,000 per week.

Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard are among the best midfielders in the Premier League. The pair have been vital in Arteta's engine room in the past few years, although Rice is set to surpass Odegaard's £260,000-per-week contract with a massive £350,000 a week deal, according to BBC Sport. That will make the England international Arsenal's joint-highest earner.

Eberechi Eze's performances for Crystal Palace and England convinced Arsenal to fork out £67.5m in the summer of 2025, and he put pen-to-paper on a four-year deal worth £200,000-per-week. Scoring five league goals against fierce rivals Tottenham in his debut season is enough to make him worth every penny for the Gunners.

The extremely versatile Mikel Merino, who has been required to play in an array of positions including striker and in defence during his Arsenal career, earns £140,000 every seven days.

Fellow World Cup winner Martin Zubimendi joined the Gunners' ranks in the summer of 2025, and the former Real Sociedad anchor - who was high on the wish lists of both Real Madrid and Liverpool - is reportedly earning around £90,000-per-week for the privilege of playing alongside Rice, Odegaard and Guimaraes.

*Declan Rice's current contract is worth £260,000 a week

It comes as no surprise that Bukayo Saka is Arsenal's highest-paid player. He signed a four-and-a-half-year deal worth a whopping £300,000-per-week in early 2026. Not a bad increase on his previous £195,000 weekly wages.

Before that deal was signed, Kai Havertz (£280,000-per-week) was making the most money at the club. His switch from Chelsea to Arsenal raised eyebrows, but was clearly a good move for the 27-year-old, professionally and financially.

Arsenal made it their goal to sign a top striker last summer and they landed on Viktor Gyokeres. The Swede is earning £220,000-per-week at the club following his £55 million move from Sporting CP.

Christos Tzolis takes home £90,000 every seven days after moving from Club Brugge, while Ethan Nwaneri's £80,000 p/w salary is currently off the books again following his loan move to Borussia Dortmund.

Noni Madueke made the surprise move from Chelsea to Arsenal last summer and is said to be making £160,000-per-week. Finally, wonderkid Max Dowman is still only on an academy scholarship contract so, per Salary Leaks, he'll earn just £350 until he turns 17. He has, however, signed a pre-agreement for a professional contract that comes into effect on his 17th birthday on December 31​ – at which point he'll be on £35,000 per week.

#1340. Why Milan have Endrick advantage over Roma and Arsenal, with €60m offer ready

Milan are prepared to offer €60m plus add-ons to buy Brazil talent Endrick from Real Madrid in January, claim Italian reports, with one very important advantage over Roma and Arsenal.

It is no secret that these three clubs are interested in picking up Endrick during the January transfer window, as the 20-year-old is frustrated at the lack of regular playing time for the Merengues.

Jose Mourinho is adamant that the youngster should not leave, but considering the loan experience at Olympique Lyonnais last season, the decision might be beyond him.

According to the Corriere dello Sport, there are two elements that put Milan at the very top of the list for the striker.

The first is that while Roma and perhaps Arsenal are only prepared to offer a loan, the Rossoneri can put €60m on the table to purchase Endrick outright, and could add some bonuses on top worth another €10m.

This could even be negotiated to give Real Madrid a buy-back clause set at €80m, giving them the option of controlling his future.

The other big element in this deal is the fact Endrick’s agency is Roc Nation.

Their ties go very deep indeed with Milan, because the new CEO of Milan Sports and Entertainment is Brett Yormark, whose twin brother Michael is President of Roc Nation.

#1339. Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”

9 - Florian Wirtz's nine chances created from open play against Brentford is the most by a player in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané v Burnley in January 2021 (9) and the most by a player in an away game since Samir Nasri v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Progress. https://t.co/xyMIQP9y5p

One of the advantages of Iraola’s Anfield appointment was his Premier League experience with Bournemouth. The Basque well knows the division and has plenty of positive memories from which to borrow.

Keith Andrews has established a clearly defined, direct style of play which speaks to Brentford’s strengths. His side are third in the Premier League for percentage of passes forward (39.2 per cent) and, coupled with the second-most high turnovers which end in a goal, Brentford have thrived off passages of organised chaos.

To play this way requires quality when you do have the ball, and full-backs Keane Lewis-Potter and Michael Kayode deserve particular praise. They have contributed materially to Brentford’s attacks, helping their side to league-high successful crosses (26) and expected goals from set-pieces (4.03).

#1338. Wayne Rooney Has Been Given New Nickname on I’m a Celeb

Former Manchester United and England striker Wayne Rooney has already been given a nickname by ITV bosses, just one show into the latest series of I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!.

The 41-year-old has bagged the biggest jungle fee of the series and made his debut in dramatic style last night. He faced his fear of heights by skydiving over the Australian coast before tucking into a thick pink liquid, which Ant and Dec dubbed a prawn star martini. He then had to transfer it into another cup to reveal a word at the bottom of his drink and secure a meal for camp.

It's safe to say it's been one of the most action-packed starts to a new series, and the Scouser has already been voted to take on Tuesday night's Bushtucker Trial, aptly named 'Jungle Food Lab'.

'Wazza' will certainly have his work cut out if he's to go one better than his wife, Coleen, who finished as a runner-up during her appearance in 2024. But it seems he's already winning over those behind the scenes, with ITV bosses having apparently taken a shine to the former footballer.

According to The Sun, ITV bosses kept Rooney's signing under wraps by giving him a codename, months before the full lineup was announced.

That name has now emerged as 'Wonder', which is a nod to the nickname he used to have in the formative years of his Premier League career.

The former Man United and England striker is heading to the jungle on November 16.

Pundits used to refer to Wazza as 'Wonder Boy' when he was just making a name for himself at Everton in the early-noughties. He famously became the youngest-ever goalscorer in Premier League history at 16, when he netted a last-minute winner for The Toffees against Arsenal in 2002.

After a career that saw him win five league titles, a Champions League as part of the 2007/08 treble-winning season, and briefly hold the title as England's record goalscorer, Rooney remains popular for his no-nonsense, often humourous punditry. There's many-a-reason he is now the shortest-ever priced celeb to win the show at 7/4.

It has also now come to light that ITV wanted Rooney to be part of last year's lineup that saw fellow Mancunians Aitch and Angry Ginge become among the two most popular celebrities.

While Wayne would have had plenty of laughs with his mates, he didn’t feel physically ready to be a part of the show. Speaking to Gabby Logan on her Life At The Midpoint Podcast, Wayne admitted he has always been self-conscious about his weight and that played a major part in him declining.

He said: “I wouldn’t have been able to do it, if I’m being honest. They asked me last year to go in and I spoke to Angry Ginge, who I know, and Aitch, who I know, and they were saying ‘come in’. Imagine the three of us in there. It would have been chaos. But I didn’t because physically I didn’t think I’d be able to."

Since snubbing the show last year, Rooney has undergone an incredible body transformation, quitting alcohol and exercising more often to shave off three stone ahead of his appearance in the Australian jungle.

#1336. The 'Real Reason' Why Ben White Refused England Call Up For Years

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

When Ben White made his England debut in 2021, it was expected that he would play a key role for his national team for many years to come.

However, he refused to play for his country for years after leaving England's camp during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. The day after England's final Group B match, it was announced that White would be returning home due to personal reasons.

Speaking in 2024, Gareth Southgate revealed that White had informed England that he did not want to be considered for selection.

White finally returned to the fold in March 2026 when he was included in Thomas Tuchel's squad for two friendly matches ahead of the World Cup.

He made his first appearance in four years against Uruguay at Wembley Stadium, coming on as a second half substitution. He was loudly booed by his own fans as he made his way onto the pitch. The Arsenal defender went on to score and give away a penalty.

It has not been made clear as to exactly why White left England's 2022 World Cup squad and made himself unavailable for selection for many years afterward.

There were rumours that White had fallen out with Southgate's assistant manager, Steve Holland. Piers Morgan has now revealed the 'real reason' why White left England's camp, giving more details of his bust-up with Holland.

Morgan said on Football Uncensored: “My view on Ben White… he’s a fantastic player. He’s been great at Arsenal, he competes with (Jurrien) Timber for the right-back (spot) but I think he’s terrific.

“He still gets booed by a section of England fans because of what happened at the Qatar World Cup in 2022, where he had this massive falling-out with Steve Holland.

“My understanding of what happened is that Holland was mocking him in front of all the players for the supposed statement that Ben White made that he doesn’t like football.

“In fact, what he said was that he doesn’t like going home and watching football after he’s been playing it all day. And he made the point this week clarifying it, that, like a lot of people, when they finish their job for the day, they don’t want to go back home and talk about it… I totally understood that.”

White returned to the England fold after Holland left the England set up alongside Southgate in 2024.

Morgan added: “Now the interesting thing about Holland is that he’s gone to Manchester United, he’s just been fired as part of the Carrick regime, he had a terrible year there, he fell out with all the players, especially Bruno Fernandes, who’s their only good player.

“So, for me, I’m totally team Ben White and the fact that he’s back in the England team is great and we should stop booing him.”

White chose not to go into detail when asked what happened in Qatar and why he made himself unavailable for England selection for many years afterward.

He told the BBC: "I think obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that. I think that is probably the best way.

"It's been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now."

When asked whether he would have done anything differently, he continued: "No, I don't think I would. Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.

"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on."

White, who is one of the highest-paid English footballers, has now made eight appearances for his country. He scored his second goal for his country in the Three Lions' 3-2 victory over world champions Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in November 2026.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'

#1334. Iconic first image of black hole holds up to scrutiny

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis.Credit: S. Lai, N. Thyagarajan, O. I. Wong and F. Diakogiannis/CSIRO

The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration wowed the world in 2019 with the first picture ever taken of a black hole’s shadow. Some researchers were unconvinced, arguing that the circular shape seen in that shot was an artefact of the team’s image-reconstruction techniques. Now, an independent group has reanalysed the EHT data, and its results, published on 11 November in Nature — including new images of the black hole — largely corroborate the original findings1.

To image black holes, the international EHT collaboration stitches together data it collects simultaneously from an array of ground-based radio telescopes that stretches across several continents. The reconstruction is extremely challenging, but in principle, the result is an image with the same level of detail, or resolution, that would be achieved with a single radio dish as wide as Earth.

Although blurry, the EHT shot of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the M87 galaxy was consistent with astrophysical models based on Albert Einstein’s general theory of relativity, which first predicted the existence of black holes. The image had a bright ring of roughly the correct radius, given what was known about the size of the black hole, with a darker disk at the centre.

However, starting in 2022, Junichiro Makino, an astrophysicist at Kobe University in Japan, and his collaborators began questioning those conclusions2. By applying one of the data-analysis techniques the EHT collaboration had used, but with slightly different assumptions, Makino’s team obtained a different result. Their image shows a glob of radio emissions rather than a ring.

#1332. Gerard Pique Issues Statement as Jesus Owono is Given Huge Ban After De Miguel's Death

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been heavily punished after he was sent off in an incident that led to the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel was left fighting for his life after a heavy collision with Owono during the match at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López on November 2.

The Spaniard was rushed to hospital after suffering a blunt cardiac injury on the pitch. He was resuscitated but passed away the following day.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) have handed Owono a 12-match ban following the incident.

They said in a statement: "The Disciplinary Committee, as an independent body within the federation's structure, has agreed to suspend Jesús Lázaro Ferrer Owono, a player for FC Andorra, for twelve matches for his actions during the CD Tenerife – FC Andorra match. Twelve matches is the maximum penalty allowed by the Disciplinary Code for the events described in the referee's report.

"The referee's report is the only document in the disciplinary proceedings file, and the Committee must determine the sanction based solely on this information. The report describes a violent action, with the leg raised and excessive force used, while the ball was in play. In light of these circumstances, the Committee has determined that the events fall under Article 102 of the Disciplinary Code.

"Furthermore, the subsequent consequences of the action, which are also documented in the referee's report and are public knowledge, have been taken into account to increase the sanction to the maximum level permitted by the regulations. Under no circumstances may the Committee exceed the threshold expressly stipulated in the applicable article."

FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique has now reacted to Owono's ban in an emotional statement. The 39-year-old is adamant that the Equatoguinean did not deserve such a heavy ban.

He said: "This Friday afternoon, we received word that the Committee had handed down a 12-game suspension to Jesús Owono. Let me be clear: Jesús will need more than 12 games before he’s available to play again. No suspension will bring Demi back to us.

"It’s been incredible to see the outpouring of support and affection from all his teammates and family members, and it’s clear that the void he’ll leave behind is enormous. It’s evident that this situation has had a massive impact, not just on Spanish football but worldwide. It’s something completely inexplicable that has never happened before in football, and even now we’re still wondering why.

"Why did this happen? Players, former players, coaches, goalkeepers... they’ve all called it an accident. I truly believe that imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús for this incident puts him in a situation he doesn’t deserve, because he isn’t to blame for any of this. My take on all this is that the 12-game suspension for Jesús Owono seems to me to be placing the blame on Jesús for consequences that weren’t his fault. I believe the penalty should be based on the action itself, not on the consequences."

Pique then referred to an incident in the match between Albacete and Sabadell earlier this month. José Corpas was given a straight red card for kicking Quadri Liameed in the head. Fortunately, Liameed did not suffer a serious injury and Corpas was only given a three-match ban as a result.

He added: "With all this in mind, my reflection is on this: What is being punished, the action or the consequences? I’m making this video because this situation has affected me very deeply on a personal level. First, I was in Tenerife when it happened, and when I went down to the locker room and saw our players’ reaction, I realised that it’s an experience that will stay with all of us who were there for the rest of our lives."

Pique then referred to an incident involving him and former Barcelona goalkeeper Victor Valdes in 2012. In their Champions League semi-final clash against Chelsea, Pique took a blow to the head after colliding with Valdes. He had to leave the pitch and woke up in hospital. Pique said Valdes wasn't to blame and that the situation with Owono was very similar.

He finished: "And we humans often need to blame someone because, otherwise, we can't understand why this happens on the field. It's an accident. I think imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús puts him in an unfair situation, because he isn't to blame for what ended up happening."

Tenerfie manager Alvaro Cervera disagrees with Pique, saying Owono's ban may seem light, but that the rules don't allow for anything else.

Owono, meanwhile, is said to be distraught following De Miguel's death. It was revealed last week that he wanted to reach out to De Miguel’s family in order to ‘share in their grief and offer his condolences in person’. It is unknown when he will return to football, if at all.

#1331. Grief-stricken Tenerife stars return to action for first time since death of Jesus de Miguel, 30, after fatal on-field collision with goalkeeper: Tributes paid and match paused in 9th minute on emotional day

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

#1330. What’s Happened to Chido Obi Since He Joined Willem II as Man Utd Consider Action

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Manchester United have several talented youngsters in their ranks at the moment, but arguably the best of the bunch is Chido Obi.

The Danish striker hit the headlines in 2023 when he scored 10 goals for Arsenal in an under-16 match against Liverpool. Obi decided that Arsenal wasn't the best team to continue his development, though, and he signed for Man Utd in the summer of 2024.

The youngster was just 17 years old when he made his debut for the Red Devils. He went onto play eight times for the first-team in the 2024/25 campaign as he looked to make his mark in the Premier League.

After failing to make a single appearance in 2025/26, Obi joined Eredivisie outfit Willem II on a season-long loan in September. United would have hoped that he could continue his development in the Netherlands and return a much better player, but things haven't worked out as they would have hoped.

Three days after signing for Willem II, Obi made his debut for the club against Excelsior. He played the final eight minutes as Willem II were beaten 3-0.

A few weeks later, he made his home debut for the club, coming on as a late substitute in a 5-1 defeat to Dutch giants Ajax. Obi put in a promising performance as he played a key role in his side's goal. He has failed to kick on from there, though.

It's been a dismal campaign so far for Willem II, who are still waiting for their first win in the Eredivisie. They are currently rock bottom of the Netherlands' top tier, having picked up just three points from their opening 12 matches. They are seven points away from safety.

Despite Willem II's struggles, Obi has struggled for game-time. He has not started a single game for the club, coming on as a second-half substitute on six occasions. He has not found the back of the net in the 71 minutes he has played.

He was given 24 minutes in his side's victory over Helmond in the Dutch Cup on October 27. After the match, caretaker boss Adrie Koster wasn't happy with his defensive efforts when Willem went down to ten men.

Koster said: "It is partly a matter of mindset, but also of youthful exuberance. That boy has never experienced anything like this before. He doesn't do it on purpose either, so we shouldn't focus everything on him. This is simply part of his learning process. But we are going to talk to him about it."

Obi's struggles have been so great that United are said to be considering recalling him in January. The Manchester Evening News report that United insert break clauses into the contracts of each young player they send on loan, and that they will consider activating the clause if Obi's situation does not improve.

Still only 18 years old, Obi still has time to fulfill his lofty potential. His spell in the Netherlands has been nothing short of a nightmare so far, though. It remains to be seen whether he can turn his fortunes around.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1328. Roma chase next Malen as they target unhappy Chelsea and Forest wingers

Il Corriere dello Sport reports that Roma are closely monitoring Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Nottingham Forest’s Callum Hudson-Odoi, hoping that a new attacking signing from the Premier League will have the same impact as Donyell Malen.

Roma are still looking for attacking reinforcement, specifically, a left winger.

According to Corriere dello Sport, two of the primary names for the Giallorossi are Chelsea’s Gittens and Forest’s Hudson-Odoi.

Both English wingers seem to be in a similar situation: unhappy with the lack of playing time at their clubs and looking for a fresh start in the January window.

This is not the first time Gittens has been linked with a move to Roma, as the Giallorossi already held talks with Chelsea last summer.

The 22-year-old has played just 55 minutes across all competitions and is recovering from an ankle injury that has kept him sidelined for over a month.

According to the report, Roma and Chelsea have stayed in contact in recent weeks, and talks could intensify soon if Roma receive guarantees about the player’s fitness.

Hudson-Odoi has only played 45 minutes in the Premier League this season, making just four league appearances. According to the report, the 26-year-old is open to a move to the Olimpico in the January window.

Barely one year ago, in January 2026, Roma signed Malen from Aston Villa on an initial loan deal with an option to buy.

Back then, the Dutchman was looking to revive his career after an inconsistent spell at Aston Villa, and his 27 goals in 34 Roma appearances prove he succeeded.

Roma hope to achieve the same with a new attacking signing from the Premier League during the 2027 January transfer window.

#1326. All 92 English Clubs Ranked By Average Attendance For the 2026/27 Season

All 92 English football clubs, from League Two to the Championship and Premier League, have been ranked by their average attendances for the 2026/27 season so far.

The results make for a fascinating read. While some of England's biggest clubs, including Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal, unsurprisingly find themselves near the top, there are certainly a few curveballs along the way.

Some clubs boasting the biggest stadiums haven't necessarily managed to pack out their impressive arenas, while a number of typically 'smaller' sides (for want of a better word) have punched above their weight and ranked higher than expected, thanks in part to their flying starts to the campaign.

Ranking at the very bottom, with an average attendance of just 1,853, are Accrington Stanley. The club's main claim to fame remains their 1989 milk advert, in which a child famously asks, “Accrington Stanley, who are they?” They rank as one of the smallest clubs in the country, but have to be given some sort of let-off for their close proximity to Manchester and Liverpool.

Barnet, Fleetwood Town - who recently knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup - and Salford City, rank just above them, with the latter being owned by some of Man United's Class of 92 but still struggling to find their own identity. This comes despite sitting top of League Two and among the favourites for another promotion.

Other notable clubs who feature in this section are Grimsby Town in 72nd, who own one of the ugliest stadiums in British football, while Swindon Town - who found themselves in the topflight in the 1993/94 season - rank two places ahead, with the Robins managing just 7,608 fans at their games this season.

English football's top-flight is one of the most closely-followed leagues in the world.

Oldham Athletic, York City and Blackpool are among several clubs in this section that have struggled to stay afloat in recent years, with all three coming perilously close to extinction because of financial troubles. Part of the problem may stem from the fact that none regularly attract more than 10,000 fans to home matches, although the wider state of the English game is a far bigger factor.

Despite enjoying three successive promotions over the last three seasons as they set their sights on reaching the Premier League sooner rather than later, Wrexham still have around 200 empty seats per match at present. They rank 54th on this list, behind the likes of Barnsley, Lincoln City and MK Dons.

Bournemouth's rise to prominence followed a similar path to Wrexham's, but they have yet to move away from their old, much smaller stadium. As a result, they boast the lowest average attendance of any Premier League side, ranking 51st overall, just one place above Luton Town, who have endured successive relegations in the opposite direction.

Brentford, who have to contend with the fact that several of their London neighbours boast much bigger fanbases, sit 42nd, behind Watford, Swansea City and Huddersfield Town.

Millwall, meanwhile, are renowned as one of the toughest clubs in English football and, alongside south London rivals Charlton Athletic, find themselves averaging just under 20,000 fans at home matches. It's a similar story for two-time FA Cup winners Portsmouth. Another side with a reputation for making plenty of noise are Stoke City, who average 22,288 in the Championship. That figure just about keeps the age-old question of 'can he do it on a cold, wet Tuesday night in Stoke?' alive and kicking.

The most incredible football stadiums on the planet - ranked in order.

Other top-flight sides in this section include Hull City in 29th, Crystal Palace in 27th and Fulham in 22nd. None of them quite manage to attract more supporters than Leicester City, however, despite the Foxes sitting 10th in the division below.

The three biggest clubs missing out on a place in the top 10 are Nottingham Forest (16th), Leeds United (13th), and Aston Villa (11th). But there is quite a jump between them and Chelsea, who just about make it in 10th with an average attendance at Stamford Bridge of 39,507.

Arsenal, top of the league as they look to retain their first Premier League title in 22 years, are surprisingly only sixth, behind both Manchester City and Liverpool. This means they also rank third in London, with Tottenham in third and West Ham in second.

But there's no surprise that Manchester United's Old Trafford, the biggest club stadium in the UK, ranks top. Fanbanter's findings suggest their attendance has increased from last term, despite the Red Devils having recently sacked Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino as they sit 18th and in the relegation zone.

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

#1323. Fabrizio Romano: Joshua Zirkzee to Hold Talks With Pochettino Over Man Utd Exit

Manchester United are already planning for the January transfer window under Mauricio Pochettino before he has even officially taken charge.

The Red Devils have appointed the Argentine to replace Michael Carrick as their manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal until 2029, having won just one of their opening 10 games in the Premier League, which has left them 18th in the table.

Pochettino is scheduled to take over on November 18th officially, with his first game in charge coming just days later against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon. But the decisions over who will be in his squad in the long-term have already begun.

Fabrizio Romano shared an update last week that stated the 54-year-old has already hold talks with the club's hierarchy over plans for the winter window, with the board expected to provide funds for him to strengthen his squad.

A left-back and a striker are believed to be the top priorities, and now speaking in his latest video on YouTube, Romano revealed that there are also conversations planned between the new gaffer and current players in the squad to discuss their future, including Joshua Zirkzee.

"Man United, in any case, want to try to get another striker in the January transfer window," he said.

"Could be an opportunity on loan, or could be a striker who can also be for the long term, depending on the opportunities, depending on the finances. But obviously, to understand the future of Joshua Zirkzee is also very important to get to the point where Man United can say, "Okay, this is the striker we want."

"Zirkzee was wanted by Juventus. Zirkzee was wanted by Fiorentina over the summer transfer window. I will not be surprised to see Italian clubs returning and jumping again on Joshua Zirkzee in the January transfer window, because there's always been interest in Zirkzee from Italy after he did fantastic at Bologna and then he joined Manchester United.

"For Zirkzee, there was also an opportunity at Everton in the final minutes of the summer transfer window, but it didn't happen because of one reason: the deal collapsing, also with Monaco and that Balogun story at the end of the summer window. So what's the situation now?

"Joshua Zirkzee is going to have a conversation with Mauricio Pochettino. Joshua Zirkzee is doing his best with Man United, and he's described as one of the best professionals at Manchester United. Always training at the best level, always doing his best for the team. But at the same time, Zirkzee wants to play.

"Zirkzee has wanted to go and play for some time now, not only in the recent weeks or months; Zirkzee wants to go because he wants to play. He loves Man United, but he feels he's not a regular starter, and he wants to play football. He wants to play regular football.

"So let's see what kind of opportunities will arrive on the table. But I will not be surprised to see Joshua Zirkzee on the move in January, unless Mauricio Pochettino can sort the situation with the boy and clarify the situation."

While it's clear that Zirkzee wasn't in the plans of Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, it remains to be seen if Pochettino has the same feeling with him.

The Netherlands international had a strong pre-season before being sidelined by Carrick, but he has scored twice in his last four appearances for the club, all coming off the substitutes bench, against Como and Aston Villa.

His technical qualities are unmatched in the squad, and if Pochettino is capable of getting him to link with the rest of the forwards in the squad, then he could be a really useful member of the squad. But if he doesn't want to be at the club, then there is no point keeping him around.

With that said, Man Utd's squad is far too thin right now, and they cannot afford to let him leave in January without replacing him first. It's imperative that any forward signing is brought in before a move for Zirkzee is sanctioned to ensure they're not left short, and the club will now have the chance to make that happen for the new manager as he looks to revolutionise Man Utd.

#1321. EURO 2028 qualifying draw: Pots, toughest opponents and ideal group for Italy

The UEFA EURO 2028 qualifying draw will take place on December 6: here’s all you need to know, including the Azzurri’s toughest opponents and their ideal group.

Italy have secured a place among the seeded teams after finishing third in their Nations League group: 54 countries participate in the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, with 24 spots available for the tournament.

There will be five pots: four containing 12 teams each and a fifth with six. Tonight’s matches will determine the final pot allocations.

The draw will result in six groups of five teams and six groups of four. The Azzurri could fall into either category. The 12 group winners and the eight highest-ranked runners-up qualify for EURO 2028.

The other four runners-up and the best-ranked Nations League teams will play for the remaining four spots in the play-offs, but there may be fewer spots available depending on how many host countries qualify.

Teams that qualify for the Nations League semi-finals will be placed in the four-team groups, and those losing in the quarter-finals will go into the five-team groups.

With four Euro 2028 co-hosts, the usual play-off path may change. UEFA could not grant automatic qualification to all four co-hosts, awarding just two spots.

If two hosts qualify through the group stage, the usual format will remain unchanged. If, however, only one qualifies for the tournament, the highest-ranked host nation that failed to qualify will be granted a place, reducing the play-offs to three paths.

If none of the hosts qualify directly, the two highest-ranked will be awarded spots, leaving only two play-off paths to determine the remaining places. However, with England among the co-hosts, this scenario seems highly unlikely.

Italy are in pot 1 alongside Spain, England, France, Belgium, Portugal, the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany, Croatia and Greece, none of which the Azzurri will meet.

The most challenging opponents from Pot 2 seem to be Switzerland, Sweden and Bosnia, not only because each of these three countries has already dealt blows to Italy in recent World Cup qualification campaigns.

Sweden beat the Azzurri in the 2018 World Cup play-off, Switzerland won the qualifying group four years later, and Bosnia beat the Azzurri in the latest World Cup play-off qualifying final this past March.

Slovakia and Scotland seem the toughest opponents from Pot 3.

Gazzetta argues that Italy’s ideal group phase would include Northern Ireland, Romania and San Marino.

Howard has caused a huge uproar after advocating for his former Everton manager, Roberto Martinez, to be the next USMNT coach. We were a Moyes Everton team, and we had a blueprint, and it worked and it was successful. He came to us and changed our entire identity. Our identity before was really good, sure. Zlatan Ibrahimovic isn't a fan of the manager put forward to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the next USMNT manager.

And if anyone thinks Ronaldo's easy to handle, ask their most recent manager. He guided it expertly. He knows World Cups. He knows club football. He knows players. It's a no-brainer for me. Howard and Martínez worked together at Everton from 2013 to 2016. The Spaniard started off his managerial career in Wales with Swansea, and worked for English clubs like Wigan and Everton.
